terms.definition: The statement an authority must publish on adopting a local plan: the adoption date, any modifications, where the plan can be inspected, the date the next plan must begin by, and the right to challenge in the High Court under section 113.

The person the Secretary of State appoints under section 15CA(3) of the 2004 Act to give observations and advice at Gateway 2 or Gateway 3 — in practice a Planning Inspector acting as gateway assessor.

For Strategic Environmental Assessment in England: Natural England, the Environment Agency and Historic England (the Historic Buildings and Monuments Commission for England). They must be consulted on the scope of the environmental report, on the report itself and told about adoption.

For an area: any spatial development strategy, the local plan, the minerals and waste plan, supplementary plans and made neighbourhood plans, together with the policies map. Planning applications must be determined in accordance with it unless material considerations indicate otherwise.

The report required by regulation 12 of the SEA Regulations, identifying, describing and evaluating the likely significant effects on the environment of implementing the plan and of reasonable alternatives, and containing the Schedule 2 information as reasonably required.
The examination of a submitted local plan by an Inspector appointed by the Secretary of State under section 15D of the 2004 Act, to decide whether it is reasonable to conclude that the plan is sound.
Modifications which, taken together, do not materially affect the contents of the plan. They are the authority's responsibility under section 15EA and are not before the Inspector.
A self-assessment of readiness to begin plan preparation, passed by publishing a self-assessment summary. No Inspectorate involvement. The day it is published is day one of the 30 months.

An assessment by an appointed person, between the second and third mandatory consultations, giving observations and advice on progress towards a sound plan, the prescribed requirements and conformity with any spatial development strategy. Done once.

A stop/go assessment by an appointed person of whether the proposed plan meets the twelve prescribed requirements in regulation 32 and the authority is ready for examination. Passing it obliges submission; failing it means repeating it.
A statement confirming the date on which the appointed person advised that each of the prescribed requirements is met.
Voluntary bodies whose activities benefit the area, bodies representing people in the area who share a protected characteristic, and bodies representing businesses in the area.

A national measure of net homes delivered against homes required over the previous three years. Below 95% triggers an action plan; below 85% a 20% buffer on the five-year supply; below 75% a deemed unmet need for the purposes of NPPF policy S5.

The minimum annual number of homes needed, calculated with the standard method in NPPF Annex D: 0.8% of existing housing stock, adjusted upwards by 0.95% for each 1% the five-year average affordability ratio is above five.

The published timetable of every key plan-making milestone, brought into effect by a statement, published in the approved data standard, checked monthly and revised the same day certain stages happen.
Published on the authority's website, available for inspection at its principal office during normal office hours, and at such other places in the area as it considers appropriate.

Changes the Inspector recommends because without them it would not be reasonable to conclude the plan is sound. Any change that materially affects a policy can only be made this way, and all must be consulted on first.

terms.term: Map of proposed local plan policies
terms.definition: The map, based on Ordnance Survey mapping, that shows where each area-specific policy in the proposed plan applies and lists the plan-wide policies. Distinct from the policies map, which covers the whole development plan after adoption.
The Inspector's framework for the examination: matters are the broad topics, issues the critical points soundness depends on, and questions what is asked to elicit the evidence.
Up to ten outcomes in the local plan, designed to monitor progress towards the vision. A prescribed requirement at Gateway 3.
The 'notice to commence': a webpage giving the authority, the area, the plan's title, where the timetable is and the date. It starts the minimum four-month notice period before Gateway 1.
A hearing at which representors speak directly to the Inspector without round-table discussion, used where there are unusually many participants or representations that do not fit topic sessions.
The Inspector's power under section 15DA to pause an examination for further work, for up to six months. Before it ends the authority must send a document setting out what has been done.
A report in year four after adoption that informs the next plan and identifies which policies and sites can be carried forward.
The map, prepared within a month of adoption and kept up to date, that illustrates the geographical application of every policy in the development plan for the area.

The twelve requirements in regulation 32 that a Gateway 3 assessor must be satisfied are met before a plan can be submitted: plan content, vision and outcomes, climate change, local nature recovery strategy, housing need, permitted content, gateway compliance and publication, regard to prescribed matters, submission documents, the policies map, and practical readiness.
The impartial person who assists the Inspector with administrative and procedural matters and is the point of contact outside hearings. Must be in post by the start of Gateway 3.

The document that sets out how the plan will be scoped, engaged on, project-managed, governed, resourced, funded and de-risked. Recommended by MHCLG and the NPPF; the Gateway 2 assessor advises on project management against it.
MHCLG's spreadsheet of red, amber and green statements for each getting-ready activity, used to decide whether to pass through Gateway 1.
The alternatives to the plan that the environmental report must identify, describe and evaluate alongside the plan itself, taking account of the plan's objectives and geographical scope.
The first mandatory consultation, after the notice to commence and before Gateway 1, on what the plan should contain and how people want to be engaged.
The Gateway 1 document setting out progress on the timetable, governance, engagement, anticipated content and SEA obligations.

NPPF policy PM15: a sound local plan is positive, appropriate, effective, consistent with national policy, and in general conformity with any adopted spatial development strategy. Applied proportionately.

The strategic tier of the development plan, produced by strategic planning authorities and the Mayor of London. A local plan must be in general conformity with an operative one, and its authority must be consulted on conformity alongside the proposed plan consultation.

The statutory and infrastructure bodies listed in regulation 2 — among them Active Travel England, the Environment Agency, Historic England, Natural England, Homes England, highway authorities, integrated care boards, utilities, the Coal Authority and neighbouring authorities — who must be invited to consultations where they may have an interest.
£993 a day (or a proportion for part of a day), the prescribed cost of an appointed person's time on gateways and examinations under the 2026 costs regulations.

A published statement, maintained with neighbouring and other relevant plan-making authorities, demonstrating that cross-boundary matters — infrastructure, unmet needs, cross-boundary growth — have been addressed where possible.

The statement setting out how the plan complies with the prescribed requirements, why regulation 11(4) is not engaged if no policies are superseded, how the plan conforms with any SDS, and where the Gateway 2 advice can be inspected. A draft helps at Gateway 2; the completed version is mandatory at Gateway 3.
The statement setting out the evidence gathered to support the plan and how it demonstrates that an examiner could reasonably conclude the plan is sound.

The environmental assessment of plans and programmes required by the Environmental Assessment of Plans and Programmes Regulations 2004, carried out during preparation and before adoption. Expected for every local plan.

A plan a local planning authority may prepare for design standards or to respond to unanticipated change at a site or group of nearby sites. It cannot subvert the local plan's vision or strategy; site allocations should be brought into the next local plan.

A statement, published with the proposed plan consultation, saying for each existing supplementary plan whether the new plan covers its matters and whether it will remain, be revoked or be requested to be revoked.

The required statement in a local plan of how the area is intended to change over the plan period, relating to its particular characteristics, with aims and objectives and up to ten measurable outcomes.

The government's expectation that a local plan is prepared and adopted within 30 months of the Gateway 1 self-assessment summary being published — months 1 to 23 preparation, 24 to 29 examination, 30 to 31 adoption.
